Fixed. The Phase 1 integration failure was caused by [HAdes/phase1_gui_tabs.py](file:///d:/X12/OFSP/HAdes/phase1_gui_tabs.py) hard-binding to `PyQt6` only, which breaks when that install has a DLL/procedure mismatch.

1. Updated [HAdes/phase1_gui_tabs.py](file:///d:/X12/OFSP/HAdes/phase1_gui_tabs.py#L9-L34) to use the same dual-backend pattern as the rest of the app: try `PyQt6`, then fallback to `PySide6` (including `Signal as pyqtSignal` compatibility).
2. Updated Phase 1 import guarding in [HAdes/HadesAI.py](file:///d:/X12/OFSP/HAdes/HadesAI.py#L152-L161) from `except ImportError` to `except Exception` so DLL/procedure loader errors are handled cleanly and logged instead of crashing import flow.
3. Verified by running `python -m py_compile HAdes/phase1_gui_tabs.py HAdes/HadesAI.py` and importing `phase1_gui_tabs` successfully.

If you still see the Windows Qt DLL error at runtime, it usually means mixed Qt installs in the same environment; this patch ensures the app can fallback to the other Qt backend instead of dying during Phase 1 tab import.
